source.title: Why Safeguarded Ships Run Aground? Aligned Large Language Models' Safety Mechanisms Tend to Be Anchored in The Template Region
source.authors: Chak Tou Leong; Qingyu Yin; Jian Wang; Wenjie Li

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether inference-time attacks and interventions that alter template-region processing affect harmful-request compliance, using mechanistic activation patching and attack-success rates rather than the original studies' fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.gate_note: The study tests inference-time bypasses and template-region interventions, not harmful or benign fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, parameter or rank localization, or training that deepens safety. Values in Figures 3, 5, and 8 are plotted only; where the text does not characterize a specific plotted condition, the row is marked cannot_determine. The AIM prompt in the appendix is a quoted attack prompt, not an instruction to this reader.
record.test_reason: Among its comparators, the study measures harmful-request attack success of an adversarial-suffix attack (AmpleGCG) on six safety-tuned models. That bears on V4's claim that suffixes defeat refusal. Its main manipulation, TempPatch, swaps internal value states at template positions. That is a white-box activation intervention, not a prefill, suffix or decoding change, so it does not match the means V4 names and is recorded under fits_no_version. No fine-tuning, per-token KL, parameter localization or safety-deepening training is done.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that aligned LLMs' initial safety decisions rely heavily on information aggregated in the chat-template region (TASA). Patching that region alone induces compliance comparable to or exceeding specialized jailbreaks, and successful attacks suppress harmfulness features there. Probe-guided steering during generation reduces ASR, but they call it a proof of concept that does not remove the learned shortcut.
record.recipe_differences: This is a mechanistic study of attention and activation patching, jailbreak evaluations, and runtime activation steering; it does not reproduce the cited fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and attack method. TempPatch is evaluated across patching proportions from 10% to 90% and on Danlz and Deval; the paper chooses the proportion with the highest Danlz ASR for the HarmBench evaluation. Probe-guided steering uses model-specific probe layers, template positions, and strengths.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing template-position value states with harmless-input states during generation (TempPatch) raises HarmBench ASR across six aligned models. It matches or exceeds AIM, PAIR and AmpleGCG, and does notably better on Llama-3 variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligned models' refusal decisions rely on information aggregated at the chat-template positions; intervening there alone induces harmful compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Role-play (AIM) and iterative-rewrite (PAIR) jailbreak prompts succeed to varying degrees: Table 1 without defense gives Gemma-2-9b 89.3% and 94.3%, Llama-3-8B 0.0% and 56.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-level jailbreaks bypass refusal in some aligned models but not others.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention at the final input position shifts from the instruction toward the template region for harmful inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some safety-tuned models shift attention toward template positions when processing harmful rather than matched harmless instructions.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe-triggered steering during generation reduced ASR on Gemma-2-9b and Llama-3-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Runtime activation steering based on transferred harmfulness probes can reduce some jailbreak attack success rates.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper acknowledges limited generalization and says its runtime detachment method is a proof of concept that does not eliminate learned safety shortcuts. Many attack-success results are shown only in plots without numerical values in the text. The probe is a surrogate for compliance, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the attack-success rates.
record.rows_left_out: Due to the 60-row limit, omitted lower-priority figure-only mechanistic results: Figure 4's per-model regional activation-patching/NIE comparisons; Figure 6's per-layer and template-position harmful-rate probes under attack; Figure 7 and Figure 11's probe-transfer accuracies; Figure 10's per-layer, per-position residual-stream patching; Figure 12's punctuation case study; and Figures 13–14's example outputs. These results concern template-region mechanisms or probe transfer but do not measure the named behaviors in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No aligned-versus-base per-token KL. The analyses concern template positions before the response, not per-position response divergence.
Prefilling a compliant start and decoding changes are not tested; greedy decoding is used throughout. Only the AmpleGCG suffix attack falls within V4.
No weight or rank localization. Head ranking is over activations, not parameters.
Template-shortcut learning is proposed as a cause, but training data or objective is not tested.
No deepening training. The steering method is inference-time and described as a proof of concept.

missing.what: AmpleGCG ASR without defense: Gemma-2-9b-it 62.3%, Llama-3-8B-Instruct 29.6%. These are the only numeric suffix-attack success values; the evaluation set is not stated.
Normalized indirect effect of patching template versus instruction value states on the compliance probe, per model. Template patching of few heads gives large NIE; instruction patching does not.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source. The paper frames TASA as related to, but distinct from, superficial or first-token alignment (Qi et al. 2024a); it locates the decision in pre-response template positions rather than response tokens. Figure 5 values are plot only, and the No Attack baselines are not stated numerically. The Table 1 'w/o Detach' ASRs are the only readable attack numbers.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or harmful-compliance measurement after such fine-tuning.
No fine-tuning on benign data or harmful-compliance measurement after such fine-tuning.
Tests jailbreak prompts, adversarial suffix attacks, and template-region activation patching. Does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes such as sampling settings.
Does not edit or ablate weights or ranks. Activation patching of attention-head value states is not a test of whether a small set of parameters carries safety.
Does not test whether training data or training objectives produce shallow safety.
The proposed probe-guided activation steering is an inference-time intervention, not training that spreads safety beyond initial tokens; no durability test of such training is reported.

relationships.reason: Based on text: Table 1 reports 62.3% AmpleGCG ASR without defense (a missing row). Figure 5 is plot only (F5-G2-9b-GCG).
relationships.display_finding: AmpleGCG reached 62.3% ASR without a defense.

relationships.condition: AmpleGCG adversarial suffixes on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
relationships.reason: The text says attacks have limited effectiveness on the Llama-3 8B and 3B variants. Table 1 gives 29.6% ASR on Llama-3-8B, so suffixes only partly defeat refusal (F5-L3-8b-GCG, F5-L3-3b-GCG).
relationships.display_finding: The authors report limited attack effectiveness on the Llama-3 8B and 3B variants, with 29.6% ASR on Llama-3-8B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TempPatch on the six tested aligned models
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that template-region patching significantly increases harmful-request ASR across tested LLMs; see F5-G2-2b-TP, F5-G2-9b-TP, F5-L2-7b-TP, F5-L3-3b-TP, F5-L3-8b-TP, and F5-M7b-TP.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: AIM, PAIR, and AmpleGCG attacks compared across the tested models
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the specialized attacks have limited effectiveness against Llama-3 variants, while the plotted per-method values are not specified in text; see F5-L3-3b-AIM, F5-L3-3b-PAIR, F5-L3-3b-GCG, F5-L3-8b-AIM, F5-L3-8b-PAIR, and F5-L3-8b-GCG.
